        "contents": "-- Migration: Create users, profiles, and teams schema with realtime support\n-- Purpose: Creates custom users table (replacing auth.users reference), profiles table, teams table\n-- Includes automatic updated_at triggers and realtime broadcasting for users table\n-- Affected tables: users, profiles, teams\n-- Special considerations: Users table is separate from auth.users, profiles reference users table\n\n-- Create profile_role enum for profiles table\ncreate type public.profile_role as enum ('student', 'team_leader', 'coach', 'admin');\n\n-- Create users table (custom table, separate from auth.users)\n-- Stores Google OAuth user data and OTP tracking\n-- Linked to auth.users via auth_user_id for authentication checks\ncreate table public.users (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  auth_user_id uuid unique references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,\n  google_email text not null unique,\n  suggested_work_email text,\n  google_profile_picture text,\n  google_full_name text,\n  last_otp_sent_at timestamptz,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null\n);\n\ncomment on table public.users is 'Custom users table storing Google OAuth user data and OTP tracking.         "contents": "Use MODDATETIME extension to set the &#96;updated_at&#96; column on every update.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\n-- Users table to sync with auth.users (Google OAuth)\n-- Note: Synced via Next.js server actions, not database triggers\ncreate table public.users (\n  id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,\n  email text not null,\n  name text,\n  picture text,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null\n);\n\n-- Role enum for profiles (authorization)\ncreate type public.profile_role as enum ('student', 'team_leader', 'coach', 'admin');\n\n-- Profiles table (pre-created by admin, linked to user after verification)\n-- Focus: Authentication and authorization only\ncreate table public.profiles (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  name text not null,\n  user_id uuid unique references public.users(id) on delete set null,  -- linked after OTP verification\n  work_email text unique not null,\n  role public.profile_role not null default 'student',\n  removed_access timestamptz,  -- null = active, set = revoked\n  removed_access_by uuid references public.profiles(id) on delete set null,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  constraint valid_czu_domain check (\n    work_email like '%@studenti.czu.cz' or work_email like '%@pef.czu.cz'\n  )\n);\n\n-- Indexes for auth queries\ncreate index profiles_user_id_idx on public.profiles(user_id);\ncreate index profiles_work_email_idx on public.profiles(work_email);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Entity Relationships\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────┐       ┌─────────────────┐\n│   auth.users    │       │    profiles     │\n│  (Supabase)     │       │  (Auth only)    │\n├─────────────────┤       ├─────────────────┤\n│ id (uuid)       │◄──┐   │ id (uuid)       │\n│ email (google)  │   │   │ name            │\n│ ...auth fields  │   └───│ user_id (1:1)   │",

        "contents": "create table public.profiles (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  name text not null,\n  picture text,  -- defaults to Google profile picture on link\n  user_id uuid unique references public.users(id) on delete set null,  -- linked after OTP verification\n  work_email text unique not null,\n  role public.profile_role not null default 'student',\n  team_id uuid references public.teams(id) on delete set null,\n  phone_number text,\n  personal_email text,\n  date_of_birth date,\n  removed_access timestamptz,  -- null = active, set = revoked\n  removed_access_by uuid references public.profiles(id) on delete set null,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  constraint valid_czu_domain check (\n    work_email like '%@studenti.czu.cz' or work_email like '%@pef.czu.cz'\n  )\n);\n\ncomment on table public.profiles is 'User profile data with role and team membership. Pre-created by admin, linked to user after OTP verification.';\n\n-- Create trigger function to automatically update updated_at column\n-- This function will be used by all tables with updated_at columns\ncreate or replace function public.handle_updated_at()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity invoker\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\nbegin\n  -- Update the updated_at column to current timestamp on any update\n  new.updated_at := now();\n  return new;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.handle_updated_at() is 'Trigger function that automatically updates the updated_at column to the current timestamp on row updates.';\n\n-- Create triggers for updated_at on all tables\ncreate trigger users_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on public.users\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_updated_at();\n\ncreate trigger teams_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on public.teams\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_updated_at();\n\ncreate trigger profiles_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on public.profiles\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_updated_at();\n\n-- Enable realtime publication for users table\nalter publication supabase_realtime add table public.users;",

        "contents": "create policy \"Users can view their own user record\" on public.users\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) );\n\n-- Users can update their own user record\ncreate policy \"Users can update their own user record\" on public.users\nfor update\nto authenticated\nusing ( auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) )\nwith check ( auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) );\n\n-- Allow authenticated users to insert their own user record (during signup)\ncreate policy \"Users can insert their own user record\" on public.users\nfor insert\nto authenticated\nwith check ( auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) );\n\n-- RLS Policies for profiles table\n-- Users can view their own profile (via user_id -&gt;         "contents": "## Architecture Overview\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    subgraph auth_flow [Authentication Flow]\n        A[User clicks Google Login] --&gt; B[Google OAuth]\n        B --&gt; C[Redirect back with Google identity]\n        C --&gt; D{Profile linked to user?}\n        D --&gt;|No| E[Prompt for work email]\n        E --&gt; F{Domain is czu.cz?}\n        F --&gt;|No| G[Show domain error]\n        G --&gt; E\n        F --&gt;|Yes| H[Send OTP to work email]\n        H --&gt; I[User enters OTP]\n        I --&gt; J{Profile exists for work email?}\n        J --&gt;|No| K[Pending Approval Page]\n        J --&gt;|Yes| L[Link profile to user]\n        D --&gt;|Yes| M{Access revoked?}\n        L --&gt; M\n        M --&gt;|Yes| N[Show access revoked]\n        M --&gt;|No| O[Grant Full Access]\n    end\n\n    subgraph request_flow [Request Validation]\n        P[Incoming Request] --&gt; Q[Middleware queries database]\n        Q --&gt; R{Profile linked to user?}\n        R --&gt;|No| S[Redirect to verify email]\n        R --&gt;|Yes| T{removed_access is null?}\n        T --&gt;|No| U[Show access revoked]\n        T --&gt;|Yes| V[Allow access]\n    end\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Validation Flow\n\n**Two-stage validation:**\n\n1. **Before OTP (Domain Check)**: Validate email ends with &#96;@studenti.czu.cz&#96; or &#96;@pef.czu.cz&#96;\n\n   - Client-side: Immediate feedback\n   - Server-side: Validated before &#96;signInWithOtp&#96; is called\n\n2. **After OTP (Profile Linking)**: Check if a profile exists for the verified work email\n\n   - If profile exists with that work_email → link profile to auth.user\n   - If no profile exists → show \"Pending Approval\" (admin must create profile first)\n   - Checked on every request via middleware\n\n## Database Schema (Supabase Migrations)\n\nTwo tables with **no RLS** - all access control is handled in Next.js:\n\n1. **&#96;users&#96;** - Custom table to sync with auth.users (Google OAuth), synced via Next.js server actions\n2. **&#96;profiles&#96;** - User authentication profile data with role and access control\n\n**Important**: No Supabase functions, triggers, or RLS policies. All business logic lives in Next.js.\n\nUse MODDATETIME extension to set the &#96;updated_at&#96; column on every update.",

        "contents": "- &#96;anon&#96;: an unauthenticated request (the user is not logged in)\n- &#96;authenticated&#96;: an authenticated request (the user is logged in)\n\nThese are actually [Postgres Roles](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/roles). You can use these roles within your Policies using the &#96;TO&#96; clause:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles are viewable by everyone\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated, anon\nusing ( true );\n\n-- OR\n\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNote that &#96;for ...&#96; must be added after the table but before the roles. &#96;to ...&#96; must be added after &#96;for ...&#96;:\n\n### Incorrect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nto authenticated\nfor select\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Correct\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Multiple operations\n\nPostgreSQL policies do not support specifying multiple operations in a single FOR clause. You need to create separate policies for each operation.\n\n### Incorrect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be created and deleted by any user\"\non profiles\nfor insert, delete -- cannot create a policy on multiple operators\nto authenticated\nwith check ( true )\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Correct\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be created by any user\"\non profiles\nfor insert\nto authenticated\nwith check ( true );\n\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be deleted by any user\"\non profiles\nfor delete\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Helper functions\n\nSupabase provides some helper functions that make it easier to write Policies.\n\n### &#96;auth.uid()&#96;\n\nReturns the ID of the user making the request.\n\n### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;\n\nReturns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:\n\n- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./supabase/migrations/20260131022000_restrict_signups_to_google_oauth.sql",

        "contents": "-- Migration: Restrict signups to Google OAuth only\n-- Purpose: Blocks email/password signups and OTP signups, only allows Google OAuth\n-- This ensures all new accounts must be created via Google OAuth\n\n-- Create before_user_created hook in public schema to only allow Google OAuth signups\n-- Blocks email/password signups and other OAuth providers\n-- Uses public schema instead of auth schema\ncreate or replace function public.before_user_created_hook(event jsonb)\nreturns jsonb\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_provider text;\n  v_encrypted_password text;\n  v_app_metadata jsonb;\n  v_identity jsonb;\n  v_has_google_identity boolean := false;\nbegin\n  -- Extract encrypted_password first (most reliable indicator of password signup)\n  v_encrypted_password := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;&gt;'encrypted_password';\n  \n  -- Block password-based signups immediately (they have encrypted_password)\n  if v_encrypted_password is not null then\n    raise exception 'Password-based signups are not allowed. Please use Google OAuth to sign in.';\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Extract provider from multiple possible locations\n  -- 1. raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'provider'\n  v_provider := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'raw_user_meta_data'-&gt;&gt;'provider';\n  \n  -- 2. app_metadata-&gt;&gt;'provider'\n  v_app_metadata := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'app_metadata';\n  if v_provider is null and v_app_metadata is not null then\n    v_provider := v_app_metadata-&gt;&gt;'provider';\n  end if;\n  \n  -- 3. Check identities array for Google provider (most reliable for OAuth)\n  if event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities' is not null then\n    for v_identity in \n      select value from jsonb_array_elements(event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities')\n    loop\n      if v_identity-&gt;&gt;'provider' = 'google' then\n        v_has_google_identity := true;\n        exit;\n      end if;\n    end loop;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Allow Google OAuth signups (check both provider variable and identities array)\n  if v_provider = 'google' or v_has_google_identity then\n    return event;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- If we reach here, it's not a Google OAuth signup and not a password signup\n  -- This must be an OTP or other email-based signup attempt",

            "text": "  ",
            "lineNumber": 32
          },
          {
            "text": "  -- 2. app_metadata-&gt;&gt;'provider'",
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "text": "  v_app_metadata := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'app_metadata';",
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "text": "  if v_provider is null and v_app_metadata is not null then",
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "text": "    v_provider := v_app_metadata-&gt;&gt;'provider';",
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "text": "  end if;",
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "text": "  ",
            "lineNumber": 38
          },
          {
            "text": "  -- 3. Check identities array for Google provider (most reliable for OAuth)",
            "lineNumber": 39
          },
          {
            "text": "  if event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities' is not null then",
            "lineNumber": 40
          },
          {
            "text": "    for v_identity in ",
            "lineNumber": 41
          },
          {
            "text": "      select value from jsonb_array_elements(event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities')",
            "lineNumber": 42
          },
          {
            "text": "    loop",
            "lineNumber": 43
          },
          {
            "text": "      if v_identity-&gt;&gt;'provider' = 'google' then",
            "lineNumber": 44
          },
          {
            "text": "        v_has_google_identity := true;",
            "lineNumber": 45
          },
          {
            "text": "        exit;",
            "lineNumber": 46
          },
          {
            "text": "      end if;",
            "lineNumber": 47
          },
          {
            "text": "    end loop;",
            "lineNumber": 48
          },
          {
            "text": "  end if;",
            "lineNumber": 49
          },
          {
            "text": "  ",
            "lineNumber": 50
          },
          {
            "text": "  -- Allow Google OAuth signups (check both provider variable and identities array)",
            "lineNumber": 51
          },
          {
            "text": "  if v_provider = 'google' or v_has_google_identity then",
            "lineNumber": 52
          },
          {
            "text": "    return event;",
            "lineNumber": 53
          },
          {
            "text": "  end if;",
            "lineNumber": 54
          },
          {
            "text": "  ",
            "lineNumber": 55
          },
          {
            "text": "  -- If we reach here, it's not a Google OAuth signup and not a password signup",
            "lineNumber": 56
          },
          {
            "text": "  -- This must be an OTP or other email-based signup attempt",
            "lineNumber": 57
          }

        "contents": "## Supabase Configuration Changes\n\nUpdate [&#96;supabase/config.toml&#96;](supabase/config.toml):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[auth]\nenable_manual_linking = true        # Required for work email linking\nenable_anonymous_sign_ins = false   # Block anonymous access\n\n[auth.email]\nenable_signup = false               # Block direct email/password signup\nenable_confirmations = false        # We use OTP for work email, not signup confirmation\n\n[auth.external.google]\nenabled = true\nclient_id = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)\"\nsecret = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Profile Verification (Next.js Middleware)\n\nAll verification logic lives in Next.js middleware, not in Supabase:\n\n- **Profile Linked**: Check &#96;profiles.user_id&#96; matches current auth.user.id\n- **Access Active**: Check &#96;profiles.removed_access IS NULL&#96;\n- **User Role**: Read &#96;profiles.role&#96; column (student, team_leader, coach, admin)\n\nThis approach:\n\n- Keeps all business logic in Next.js (single source of truth)\n- Allows real-time updates (e.g., instant access revocation)\n- Admin pre-creates profiles, users link via work email verification\n- Supabase only handles auth + data storage (no custom hooks or functions)\n\n## Development &amp; Testing with Supabase MCP\n\nThe project has a &#96;supabase/&#96; directory with Supabase MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration available for:\n\n1. **Running migrations**: Apply and test database schema changes locally\n2. **Debugging auth flow**: Inspect user sessions and profile data\n3. **Testing verification logic**: Query profiles table for auth checks\n\n**Useful MCP commands for development:**\n\n- Seed test data into profiles table for auth testing\n- Inspect auth.users and profiles tables\n- Test profile linking and access revocation queries\n\n## Key Security Features\n\n### Supabase (Data Layer Only)\n\n1. **Database Constraints**:\n\n   - Domain constraint ensures only valid CZU domains in profiles\n   - Unique constraints on work_email, user_id\n\n2. **No RLS or Functions**:\n\n   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions",

        "contents": "### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;\n\nReturns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:\n\n- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.\n- &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; - cannot be updated by the user, so it's a good place to store authorization data.\n\nThe &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function is extremely versatile. For example, if you store some team data inside &#96;app_metadata&#96;, you can use it to determine whether a particular user belongs to a team. For example, if this was an array of IDs:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"User is in team\"\non my_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( team_id in (select auth.jwt() -&gt; 'app_metadata' -&gt; 'teams'));\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### MFA\n\nThe &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function can be used to check for [Multi-Factor Authentication](mdc:docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa#enforce-rules-for-mfa-logins). For example, you could restrict a user from updating their profile unless they have at least 2 levels of authentication (Assurance Level 2):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Restrict updates.\"\non profiles\nas restrictive\nfor update\nto authenticated using (\n  (select auth.jwt()-&gt;&gt;'aal') = 'aal2'\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## RLS performance recommendations\n\nEvery authorization system has an impact on performance. While row level security is powerful, the performance impact is important to keep in mind. This is especially true for queries that scan every row in a table - like many &#96;select&#96; operations, including those using limit, offset, and ordering.\n\nBased on a series of [tests](mdc:https:/github.com/GaryAustin1/RLS-Performance), we have a few recommendations for RLS:\n\n### Add indexes\n\nMake sure you've added [indexes](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/indexes) on any columns used within the Policies which are not already indexed (or primary keys). For a Policy like this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table",

For example, instead of this query:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on rls_test\nusing ( auth.uid() = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nUse:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on rls_test\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis prevents the policy &#96;( (select auth.uid()) = user_id )&#96; from running for any &#96;anon&#96; users, since the execution stops at the &#96;to authenticated&#96; step.",

        "contents": "await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,\n    picture: user.user_metadata.avatar_url  // Default to Google picture\n  })\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 4: Middleware Validation\n\nQuery database for profile linked to current auth.user and check &#96;removed_access IS NULL&#96; on every request to protected routes.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Middleware check\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id, role, removed_access')\n  .eq('user_id', user.id)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) redirect('/auth/verify-work-email');\nif (profile.removed_access) redirect('/auth/access-revoked');\n// User has active access, continue...\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Estimated Complexity\n\n| Task | Complexity | Lines of Code |\n\n|------|------------|---------------|\n\n| Delete old auth files | Trivial | -500 lines |\n\n| Security lockdown config | Trivial | ~20 lines TOML |\n\n| Database migration | Low | ~40 lines SQL (users, profiles, indexes) |\n\n| Constants + validation | Trivial | ~25 lines |\n\n| Server actions (auth logic) | Medium | ~60 lines |\n\n| Middleware update | Medium | ~50 lines (includes DB queries) |\n\n| Google login page | Low | ~30 lines |\n\n| Work email form + linking | Medium | ~120 lines |\n\n| Pending approval page | Low | ~20 lines |\n\n| Access revoked page | Low | ~20 lines |\n\n**Total new code**: ~385 lines (vs ~500 lines deleted)\n\n## Separation of Concerns\n\n### Supabase (Auth + Storage Only)\n\n- **Authentication**: Google OAuth flow, session management, OTP emails\n- **Database**: Store profiles and users data (no RLS - Next.js handles access control)\n- **No business logic**: No custom hooks, no stored procedures, no triggers, no functions\n\n### Next.js (All Business Logic)\n\n- **Middleware**: Profile verification, access checks, role-based routing\n- **Server Actions**: Profile linking, access revocation\n- **Validation**: Domain validation, input sanitization, business rules\n- **Authorization**: Role hierarchy checks, permission enforcement\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                         Next.js                                  │",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

            "text": "  .from('profiles')",

          {

          {

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 335
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript",

          },
          {
            "text": "// Middleware check",

          },
          {
            "text": "const { data: profile } = await supabase",

          },
          {
            "text": "  .from('profiles')",

          },
          {
            "text": "  .select('id, role, removed_access')",
            "lineNumber": 340
          },
          {
            "text": "  .eq('user_id', user.id)",

            "text": "  .single();",

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 348
          },
          {
            "text": "## Estimated Complexity",
            "lineNumber": 349
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 350
          },
          {
            "text": "| Task | Complexity | Lines of Code |",

          },
          {

          },

          },

          {
            "text": "**Total new code**: ~385 lines (vs ~500 lines deleted)",
            "lineNumber": 375
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 376
          },
          {
            "text": "## Separation of Concerns",
            "lineNumber": 377
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 378
          },
          {
            "text": "### Supabase (Auth + Storage Only)",
            "lineNumber": 379
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 380
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Authentication**: Google OAuth flow, session management, OTP emails",
            "lineNumber": 381
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Database**: Store profiles and users data (no RLS - Next.js handles access control)",
            "lineNumber": 382
          },
          {
            "text": "- **No business logic**: No custom hooks, no stored procedures, no triggers, no functions",
            "lineNumber": 383
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 384
          },
          {
            "text": "### Next.js (All Business Logic)",
            "lineNumber": 385
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 386
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 387
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Server Actions**: Profile linking, access revocation",
            "lineNumber": 388
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Validation**: Domain validation, input sanitization, business rules",
            "lineNumber": 389
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Authorization**: Role hierarchy checks, permission enforcement",
            "lineNumber": 390
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",

          },
          {
            "text": "┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐",

{\n    try {\n      // Application logic: validation, auth, delegation\n      const result = await createUser({\n        userId: ctx.auth.userId,\n        ...input\n      });\n      \n      return { success: true, data: result };\n    } catch (error) {\n      // Application logic: error handling\n      if (error instanceof CustomError) {\n        throw error;\n      }\n      throw new CustomError(\"INTERNAL_ERROR\", \"An unexpected error occurred\");\n    }\n  });\n\n// Business Logic (Service Layer)\nexport const createUser = async (params: CreateUserParams): Promise&lt;User&gt; =&gt; {\n  const { userId, email, name, role } = params;\n  \n  // Business logic: domain rules\n  if (role === 'admin' &amp;&amp; !await hasAdminPrivileges(userId)) {\n    throw new CustomError(\"UNAUTHORIZED\", \"Insufficient privileges for admin role\", 403);\n  }\n  \n  // Business logic: business validations\n  if (await isEmailAlreadyTaken(email)) {\n    throw new CustomError(\"CONFLICT\", \"Email already registered\", 409);\n  }\n  \n  // Business logic: domain operations\n  const user = await userRepo.create({\n    email: email.toLowerCase(),\n    name: name.trim(),\n    role,\n    status: 'pending_verification'\n  });\n  \n  // Business logic: business workflow\n  await sendWelcomeEmail(user);\n  await createDefaultPreferences(user.id);\n  \n  return user;\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### External API Integration\n\n- Isolate external service calls in dedicated modules\n- Implement retry logic with exponential backoff\n- Map provider errors to internal error types\n- Store sensitive data (tokens, keys) securely\n\n## Database &amp;         "contents": "-- Grant execute permission to authenticated and anonymous roles\n-- This allows the trigger to execute when users update their email\ngrant execute on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() to authenticated;\ngrant execute on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() to anon;\n\n-- Create trigger on auth.users table\n-- This fires BEFORE any update to email or email_change columns\n-- The trigger cannot be bypassed - it runs at the database level\ndrop trigger if exists validate_czu_email_domain_trigger on auth.users;\n\ncreate trigger validate_czu_email_domain_trigger\nbefore update of email, email_change on auth.users\nfor each row\nexecute function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger();\n\n-- Add comment explaining the security model\ncomment on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() is \n'Server-side trigger function that validates email domains at the database level. Uses SECURITY DEFINER to access auth.users table. Cannot be bypassed by client-side code.       "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./.cursor/rules/create-rls-policies.mdc",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 43

        },
        "contents": "---\ndescription: Guidelines for writing Postgres Row Level Security policies\nalwaysApply: false\n---\n\n# Database: Create RLS policies\n\nYou're a Supabase Postgres expert in writing row level security policies. Your purpose is to generate a policy with the constraints given by the user. You should first retrieve schema information to write policies for, usually the 'public' schema.\n\nThe output should use the following instructions:\n\n- The generated SQL must be valid SQL.\n- You can use only CREATE POLICY or ALTER POLICY queries, no other queries are allowed.\n- Always use double apostrophe in SQL strings (eg. 'Night''s watch')\n- You can add short explanations to your messages.\n- The result should be a valid markdown. The SQL code should be wrapped in &#96;&#96;&#96; (including sql language tag).\n- Always use \"auth.uid()\" instead of \"current_user\".\n- SELECT policies should always have USING but not WITH CHECK\n- INSERT policies should always have WITH CHECK but not USING\n- UPDATE policies should always have WITH CHECK and most often have USING\n- DELETE policies should always have USING but not WITH CHECK\n- Don't use &#96;FOR ALL&#96;. Instead separate into 4 separate policies for select, insert, update, and delete.\n- The policy name should be short but detailed text explaining the policy, enclosed in double quotes.\n- Always put explanations as separate text. Never use inline SQL comments.\n- If the user asks for something that's not related to SQL policies, explain to the user\n  that you can only help with policies.\n- Discourage &#96;RESTRICTIVE&#96; policies and encourage &#96;PERMISSIVE&#96; policies, and explain why.\n\nThe output should look like this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE POLICY \"My descriptive policy.\" ON books FOR INSERT to authenticated USING ( (select auth.uid()) = author_id ) WITH ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nSince you are running in a Supabase environment, take note of these Supabase-specific additions below.\n\n## Authenticated and unauthenticated roles\n\nSupabase maps every request to one of the roles:\n\n- &#96;anon&#96;: an unauthenticated request (the user is not logged in)\n- &#96;authenticated&#96;: an authenticated request (the user is logged in)",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 1
          },
          {
            "text": "description: Guidelines for writing Postgres Row Level Security policies",
            "lineNumber": 2
          },
          {
            "text": "alwaysApply: false",
            "lineNumber": 3
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 4
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 5
          },
          {
            "text": "# Database: Create RLS policies",
            "lineNumber": 6
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 7
          },
          {
            "text": "You're a Supabase Postgres expert in writing row level security policies. Your purpose is to generate a policy with the constraints given by the user. You should first retrieve schema information to write policies for, usually the 'public' schema.",
            "lineNumber": 8
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 9
          },
          {
            "text": "The output should use the following instructions:",
            "lineNumber": 10
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 11
          },
          {
            "text": "- The generated SQL must be valid SQL.",
            "lineNumber": 12
          },
          {
            "text": "- You can use only CREATE POLICY or ALTER POLICY queries, no other queries are allowed.",
            "lineNumber": 13
          },
          {
            "text": "- Always use double apostrophe in SQL strings (eg. 'Night''s watch')",
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "text": "- You can add short explanations to your messages.",
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "text": "- The result should be a valid markdown. The SQL code should be wrapped in &#96;&#96;&#96; (including sql language tag).",
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "text": "- Always use \"auth.uid()\" instead of \"current_user\".",
            "lineNumber": 17
          },
          {
            "text": "- SELECT policies should always have USING but not WITH CHECK",
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "text": "- INSERT policies should always have WITH CHECK but not USING",
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "text": "- UPDATE policies should always have WITH CHECK and most often have USING",
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "text": "- DELETE policies should always have USING but not WITH CHECK",
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "text": "- Don't use &#96;FOR ALL&#96;. Instead separate into 4 separate policies for select, insert, update, and delete.",
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "text": "- The policy name should be short but detailed text explaining the policy, enclosed in double quotes.",
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "- Always put explanations as separate text. Never use inline SQL comments.",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "text": "- If the user asks for something that's not related to SQL policies, explain to the user",
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "text": "  that you can only help with policies.",
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "text": "- Discourage &#96;RESTRICTIVE&#96; policies and encourage &#96;PERMISSIVE&#96; policies, and explain why.",
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "text": "The output should look like this:",
            "lineNumber": 29
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 30
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "text": "CREATE POLICY \"My descriptive policy.\" ON books FOR INSERT to authenticated USING ( (select auth.uid()) = author_id ) WITH ( true );",
            "lineNumber": 32
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "text": "Since you are running in a Supabase environment, take note of these Supabase-specific additions below.",
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "text": "## Authenticated and unauthenticated roles",
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 38
          },
          {
            "text": "Supabase maps every request to one of the roles:",
            "lineNumber": 39
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 40
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;anon&#96;: an unauthenticated request (the user is not logged in)",
            "lineNumber": 41
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;authenticated&#96;: an authenticated request (the user is logged in)",
            "lineNumber": 42
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.230929896235466

        "contents": "   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions\n   - All access control handled by Next.js\n\n### Next.js (Application Layer - All Business Logic)\n\n1. **Middleware Verification**:\n\n   - Queries &#96;profiles&#96; table for linked user_id\n   - Checks &#96;removed_access&#96; is null for active access\n   - Enforces role-based route protection\n   - Real-time verification (instant access revocation)\n\n2. **Domain Validation** (in server actions):\n\n   - Client-side validation for UX (immediate feedback)\n   - Server-side validation before sending OTP\n   - Validates email format and CZU domain\n\n3. **Access Management** (in server actions):\n\n   - Admin sets &#96;removed_access&#96; timestamp and &#96;removed_access_by&#96; profile\n   - Immediate effect on next request\n   - Audit trail of who revoked access and when\n\n## Authentication Flow Details\n\n### Step 1: Google Login\n\nUser clicks Google login button, Supabase handles OAuth flow.\n\n### Step 2: Work Email Input with Domain Validation\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Validate domain before sending OTP\nif (!isValidWorkEmailDomain(workEmail)) {\n  throw new Error('Email must be @studenti.czu.cz or @pef.czu.cz');\n}\n\n// Send OTP to work email (only after domain validation passes)\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  options: { shouldCreateUser: false }\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 3: OTP Verification and Profile Linking\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// After user enters OTP, verify it\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  token: otpCode,\n  type: 'email'\n});\n\n// Check if profile exists for this work email\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id')\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) {\n  // No profile exists - redirect to pending approval\n  redirect('/auth/pending-approval');\n}\n\n// Link profile to current user\nconst { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\nawait supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,",

        "contents": "  v_email_change text;\n  v_domain text;\nbegin\n  -- Only validate on UPDATE (email changes), not INSERT (new user creation)\n  -- This allows OAuth signups (Google, etc.) to create accounts with any email\n  if tg_op != 'UPDATE' then\n    return NEW;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Validate email_change field (where Supabase stores new email during change process)\n  -- This applies to ALL users (both OAuth and email-only)\n  -- OAuth users can sign up, but when they try to add an email identity, it must be CZU domain\n  if OLD.email_change is distinct from NEW.email_change then\n    v_email_change := NEW.email_change;\n    \n    -- Skip validation if email_change is null or empty\n    if v_email_change is not null and v_email_change != '' then\n      -- Extract domain from email_change (everything after @)\n      v_domain := lower(split_part(v_email_change, '@', 2));\n      \n      -- Validate domain is one of the allowed CZU domains\n      -- This applies to all users, including OAuth users trying to add email identity\n      if v_domain not in ('pef.czu.cz', 'studenti.czu.cz') then\n        raise exception 'Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz. Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Validate email field if it changed\n  -- For OAuth users: validate when they're changing from OAuth email to a new email\n  -- For email-only users: always validate\n  if OLD.email is distinct from NEW.email then\n    v_email := NEW.email;\n    \n    -- Skip validation if email is null or empty\n    if v_email is not null and v_email != '' then\n      -- Extract domain from email (everything after @)\n      v_domain := lower(split_part(v_email, '@', 2));\n      \n      -- Validate domain is one of the allowed CZU domains\n      -- This applies to all users when changing primary email\n      if v_domain not in ('pef.czu.cz', 'studenti.czu.cz') then\n        raise exception 'Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz. Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  return NEW;\nend;\n$$;\n\n-- Grant execute permission to authenticated and anonymous roles\n-- This allows the trigger to execute when users update their email",

        "contents": "-- Migration: Create trigger function to populate public.users on auth.users creation\n-- Purpose: Automatically creates a row in public.users table when a new user is created in auth.users\n-- This ensures that every authenticated user has a corresponding record in public.users with their Google OAuth data\n-- Affected tables: public.users\n-- Special considerations: Uses SECURITY DEFINER to access auth.users table, extracts Google OAuth metadata\n-- IMPORTANT: This migration must be run through Supabase Dashboard SQL Editor or with service_role key\n--            to ensure proper privileges for creating triggers on auth.users table\n\n-- Create trigger function to populate public.users table when auth.users is created\n-- Extracts Google OAuth data from auth.users.raw_user_meta_data and auth.users.email\n-- Uses SECURITY DEFINER to allow access to auth.users table\n-- Function is created in public schema (matching pattern from validate_czu_email_domain migration)\ncreate or replace function public.handle_new_auth_user()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = public, auth\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_google_email text;\n  v_google_full_name text;\n  v_google_profile_picture text;\n  v_raw_meta_data jsonb;\nbegin\n  -- Extract raw_user_meta_data (contains Google OAuth profile information)",

        "contents": "-- Migration: Server-side CZU email domain validation\n-- Purpose: Ensures that email addresses being changed must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz\n-- This uses SECURITY DEFINER to create a trigger on auth.users table for true server-side enforcement\n-- The trigger runs at the database level and cannot be bypassed by client-side code\n\n-- Create validation trigger function with SECURITY DEFINER\n-- SECURITY DEFINER allows the function to access auth.users table even when called by regular users\n-- This provides true server-side enforcement at the Supabase database level\ncreate or replace function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = public, auth\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_email text;\n  v_email_change text;\n  v_domain text;\nbegin\n  -- Only validate on UPDATE (email changes), not INSERT (new user creation)",

        "contents": "-- Enable realtime publication for users table\nalter publication supabase_realtime add table public.users;\n\n-- Create trigger function for realtime broadcasting on users table\n-- Uses realtime.broadcast_changes for database change notifications\ncreate or replace function public.users_realtime_broadcast_trigger()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\nbegin\n  -- Broadcast changes to users table using dedicated topic pattern\n  -- Topic format: users:{user_id} for user-specific updates\n  perform realtime.broadcast_changes(\n    tg_table_name || ':' || coalesce(new.id, old.id)::text,\n    tg_op,\n    tg_op,\n    tg_table_name,\n    tg_table_schema,\n    new,\n    old\n  );\n  return coalesce(new, old);\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.users_realtime_broadcast_trigger() is 'Trigger function that broadcasts changes to the users table via Supabase Realtime. Uses dedicated topic pattern users:{user_id}.';\n\n-- Create trigger for realtime broadcasting on users table\ncreate trigger users_realtime_broadcast_trigger\nafter insert or update or delete on public.users\nfor each row\nexecute function public.users_realtime_broadcast_trigger();\n\n-- Create indexes for common queries\ncreate index profiles_user_id_idx on public.profiles(user_id);\ncreate index profiles_work_email_idx on public.profiles(work_email);\ncreate index profiles_team_id_idx on public.profiles(team_id);\ncreate index users_google_email_idx on public.users(google_email);\ncreate index users_suggested_work_email_idx on public.users(suggested_work_email);\ncreate index users_auth_user_id_idx on public.users(auth_user_id);\n\n-- Enable Row Level Security on all tables\nalter table public.users enable row level security;\nalter table public.profiles enable row level security;\nalter table public.teams enable row level security;\n\n-- RLS Policies for users table\n-- Users can view their own user record (via auth_user_id link to auth.users)\ncreate policy \"Users can view their own user record\" on public.users\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) );",

      "codeBlock": {

        "contents": "begin\n  -- Extract raw_user_meta_data (contains Google OAuth profile information)\n  v_raw_meta_data := new.raw_user_meta_data;\n  \n  -- Extract email from auth.users.email (primary email field)\n  -- Fallback to raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'email' if needed\n  v_google_email := coalesce(new.email, v_raw_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'email');\n  \n  -- Extract Google OAuth profile data from raw_user_meta_data\n  -- Google OAuth typically provides: full_name, avatar_url (or picture), email\n  v_google_full_name := v_raw_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'full_name';\n  v_google_profile_picture := coalesce(\n    v_raw_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'avatar_url',\n    v_raw_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'picture'\n  );\n  \n  -- Insert new row into public.users table with extracted data\n  -- auth_user_id links to auth.users.id for authentication checks\n  insert into public.users (\n    auth_user_id,\n    google_email,\n    google_full_name,\n    google_profile_picture\n  )\n  values (\n    new.id,\n    v_google_email,\n    v_google_full_name,\n    v_google_profile_picture\n  );\n  \n  return new;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.handle_new_auth_user() is 'Trigger function that automatically creates a row in public.users table when a new user is created in auth.users. Extracts Google OAuth profile data (email, full_name, profile_picture) from auth.users.raw_user_meta_data and populates the public.users table. Uses SECURITY DEFINER to access auth.users table.';\n\n-- Grant execute permission to authenticated and anonymous roles\n-- This allows the trigger to execute when new users are created\ngrant execute on function public.handle_new_auth_user() to authenticated;\ngrant execute on function public.handle_new_auth_user() to anon;\n\n-- Create trigger on auth.users table\n-- Fires AFTER INSERT to ensure the auth.users row is fully created before populating public.users\n-- Drop trigger if it exists to allow idempotent migrations\n-- NOTE: Creating triggers on auth.users requires ownership or superuser privileges\n--       Run this migration through Supabase Dashboard SQL Editor for proper permissions\ndrop trigger if exists on_auth_user_created on auth.users;",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./.cursor/rules/use-realtime.mdc",
        "range": {

        "contents": "SECURITY DEFINER\nLANGUAGE plpgsql\nAS $$\nBEGIN\n  PERFORM realtime.send(\n    'room:' || NEW.room_id::text,\n    'status_changed',\n    jsonb_build_object('id', NEW.id, 'status', NEW.status),\n    false\n  );\n  RETURN NEW;\nEND;\n$$;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nThis allows us to broadcast to a specific room with any content that is not bound to a table or if you need to send data to public channels. It's also a good way to integrate with other services and extensions.\n\n### Conditional Broadcasting\nIf you need to broadcast only significant changes, you can use the following pattern:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\n-- Only broadcast significant changes\nIF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.status IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.status THEN\n  PERFORM realtime.broadcast_changes(\n    'room:' || NEW.room_id::text,\n    TG_OP,\n    TG_OP,\n    TG_TABLE_NAME,\n    TG_TABLE_SCHEMA,\n    NEW,\n    OLD\n  );\nEND IF;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nThis is just an example as you can use any logic you want that is SQL compatible.\n\n## Authorization Setup\n\n### Basic RLS Setup\nTo access a private channel you need to set RLS policies against &#96;realtime.messages&#96; table for SELECT operations.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\n-- Simple policy with indexed columns\nCREATE POLICY \"room_members_can_read\" ON realtime.messages\nFOR SELECT TO authenticated\nUSING (\n  topic LIKE 'room:%' AND\n  EXISTS (\n    SELECT 1 FROM room_members\n    WHERE user_id = auth.uid()\n    AND room_id = SPLIT_PART(topic, ':', 2)::uuid\n  )\n);\n\n-- Required index for performance\nCREATE INDEX idx_room_members_user_room\nON room_members(user_id, room_id);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nTo write to a private channel you need to set RLS policies against &#96;realtime.messages&#96; table for INSERT operations.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\n-- Simple policy with indexed columns\nCREATE POLICY \"room_members_can_write\" ON realtime.messages\nFOR INSERT TO authenticated\nUSING (\n  topic LIKE 'room:%' AND\n  EXISTS (\n    SELECT 1 FROM room_members\n    WHERE user_id = auth.uid()\n    AND room_id = SPLIT_PART(topic, ':', 2)::uuid\n  )\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Client Authorization\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nconst channel = supabase.channel('room:123:messages', {\n  config: { private: true }\n})\n  .on('broadcast', { event: 'message_created' }, handleMessage)",

        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "/**\n * Checks if the authenticated user has an email identity linked\n * (not just OAuth providers like Google)\n * @returns true if user has an email identity, false otherwise\n */\nexport async function hasEmailIdentity(): Promise&lt;boolean&gt; {\n  const supabase = await createClient();\n  const { data: { user }, error } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n\n  if (error || !user) {\n    return false;\n  }\n\n  // Check if user has an email identity (not just OAuth)\n  // User identities include: email, google, etc.\n  // We need at least one email identity\n  const identities = user.identities || [];\n  \n  // Check if any identity is an email identity (not OAuth)\n  return identities.some(\n    (identity) =&gt; identity.provider === \"email\"\n  );\n}",
